question.value: Improve the laboratory rotational spectroscopic parameters of mono-deuterated oxirane ($c$-C$_2$H$_3$DO) and use the updated rest frequencies to detect it and determine its abundance and deuteration ratio towards IRAS 16293$-$2422 B.

evidence.quote: We prepared a sample of mono-deuterated oxirane and studied its rotational spectrum in the laboratory between 490 GHz and 1060 GHz in order to improve its spectroscopic parameters and consequently the calculated rest frequencies of its rotational transitions.

provided.value: Laboratory rotational spectra of c-C2H3DO between 490 and 1060 GHz using a 5 m Pyrex cell, VDI frequency multipliers driven by a Rhode & Schwarz SMF 100A synthesizer, and an InSb bolometer

evidence.quote: The measurements were carried out at room temperature in a 5 m long single path Pyrex glass cell equipped with high-density polyethylene windows.

Two frequency multipliers (VDI Inc.) driven by a Rhode & Schwarz SMF 100A microwave synthesizer were used as sources in the region 490$-$1060 GHz. A closed cycle liquid He-cooled InSb bolometer (QMC Instruments Ltd) was employed as a detector.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit laboratory rotational transitions and calculate rest frequencies and spectroscopic parameters of c-C2H3DO

method.value: Global least-squares fitting of new submillimetre laboratory transitions (490-750 GHz and 810-1060 GHz) combined with previous MW, mmW, and recalibrated FIR data using Watson's S reduction (III^l representation) and A reduction (I^r representation).

evidence.quote: Fitting and calculation of $c$-C$_2$H$_3$DO transition frequencies was performed with Pickett’s SPFIT and SPCAT programmes (cite: spfit_1991).

evidence.loc: Discussion of the laboratory spectroscopic results
evidence.quote: The parameter set in the III$^l$ representation employing Watson’s S reduction should be favoured over the set in the I$^r$ representation employing the A reduction because two fewer parameters are needed for a satisfactory fit.

key_parameters.value: 1504 new sub-mmW transitions (1091 frequencies) in 490-750 GHz and 810-1060 GHz; global fit of 2416 transitions (1613 frequencies) with J_max = 58, K_a,max = 43, K_c,max = 56

evidence.quote: Trial fits with the aim to minimize the average shift yielded a recalibration factor of 1.0000037.

assumptions.value: Dipole moment components derived from structure: mu_a = 0.36 D, mu_b = 1.86 D, mu_c = 0.08 D

evidence.quote: We derived from the structural parameters of the molecule that the rotation of the principal inertial axis system of $c$-C$_2$H$_3$DO with respect to that of $c$-C$_2$H$_4$O leads to a small $\mu _a$ dipole moment component of 0.36 D, a very small $\mu _c = 0.08$ D and an almost unchanged $\mu _b = 1.86$ D.

assumptions.value: Assigned uncertainties: 50 kHz for MW data, 5 kHz for mmW data, 0.00008 cm^-1 for FIR data, and 5 to 50 kHz for new sub-mmW lines

method.value: Calculate LTE synthetic spectra using updated c-C2H3DO rest frequencies (from S reduction, III^l representation) and fit to ALMA PILS Band 7 and Band 6 spectra at the offset position of IRAS 16293-2422 B.

assumptions.value: Local thermodynamical equilibrium (LTE) and 4 equivalent H atoms in c-C2H4O for D-to-H conversion

analysis_steps.goal: Construct rotation diagram to independently derive rotational temperature and column density

method.value: Fit a rotation diagram to the unblended or slightly blended c-C2H3DO transitions spanning a range of upper state energies (33 to 122 K).

evidence.quote: We constructed a rotation diagram from the unblended or only slightly blended transitions because these were numerous enough and span a range of upper state energies as can be seen in Table [1](#tab_obs-lines).

Fits of the detected lines using the rotation diagrams yield a temperature of $T_{\rm rot} = 103 \pm 19$ K, which in turn agrees well with 125 K derived for the $c$-C$_2$H$_4$O main isotopologue previously.

assumptions.value: LTE optically thin lines (standard rotation diagram assumption)

evidence.quote: Such a rotation diagram may serve as a check of the modelling and it also provides a measure of the statistical uncertainties originating from the observational data.

fitting.value: Linear fit to rotation diagram yielding T_rot and column density with statistical uncertainties

evidence.quote: The temperature of $103 \pm 19$ K determined from the rotation diagram $c$-C$_2$H$_3$DO agrees well with the 125 K obtained for $c$-C$_2$H$_4$O (cite: PILS_COMs_2017). The column density from the rotation diagram of $(7.8 \pm 1.5) \times 10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ is slightly lower than $8.9 \times 10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ derived from the modelling applying 125 K

findings_qualitative.value: Mono-deuterated oxirane (c-C2H3DO) is detected for the first time in the interstellar medium towards IRAS 16293-2422 B.

evidence.quote: The updated rest frequencies were employed to detect $c$-C$_2$H$_3$DO for the first time in the interstellar medium in the Atacama Large Millimetre/submillimetre Array (ALMA) Protostellar Interferometric Line Survey (PILS) of the Class 0 protostellar system IRAS 16293$-$242.

findings_qualitative.value: The D-to-H ratio per H atom of oxirane (~0.036) is slightly higher than species such as methanol, formaldehyde, and ketene (0.02-0.03), but lower than larger complex organics such as ethanol, methylformate, and glycolaldehyde (0.05-0.06), suggesting oxirane forms fairly early in prestellar core evolution.

evidence.quote: The degree of deuteration of $c$-C$_2$H$_3$DO referenced to one H atom of $\sim$0.036 is slightly larger than species such as formaldehyde, methanol, ketene, HNCO, formamide and cyanamide with ratios of 0.02–0.03 but lower than some of the larger complex species such as ethanol, methylformate, glycolaldehyde and acetaldehyde with ratios of 0.05–0.06 (cite: PILS_div-isos_2018; PILS_formamide_2016; PILS_cyanamide_2018).
This difference may reflect differences in the formation time with the species with the lower ratios forming earlier in the evolution of the prestellar cores.

findings_qualitative.value: Doubly-deuterated oxirane isotopomers may be detectable in the PILS data if their deuteration degree is enhanced similarly to other multiply deuterated molecules (yielding ratios of 0.01 to 0.025 relative to the main species) and if lines are not severely blended.

evidence.quote: If the deuteration of the three dideutero-oxirane isotopomers is enhanced in a similar way compared with that of monodeutero-oxirane we may observe column density ratios of 0.01 to 0.025 for each of the three dideutero-oxirane isotopomers compared to the main species, which may be enough for identifications provided not all of the stronger lines of these three species are blended with stronger lines of other species.

claims.hypothesis: Measuring the submillimetre rotational spectrum of c-C2H3DO between 490 and 1060 GHz will resolve velocity/frequency deviations in astronomical lines and yield accurate spectroscopic parameters up to the terahertz regime.
claims.experiment: Synthesized c-C2H3DO, recorded 1504 submillimetre transitions in 490-750 GHz and 810-1060 GHz, and performed a global fit with previous MW, mmW, and recalibrated FIR data using SPFIT.
claims.result: Determined full sets of spectroscopic parameters up to eighth order plus decic parameters with a global rms error of 0.892 (S reduction, III^l), resolving ~0.2-0.3 MHz deviations in oblate-paired transitions in the PILS frequency range.
claims.finding: The improved spectroscopic parameter set provides transition frequencies sufficiently accurate up to at least 1.5 THz for astronomical searches.

evidence.quote: Releasing different sets of sextic distortion parameters resulted in transition frequencies that differed by around 0.2 MHz for the lines we had identified in our astronomical data, significant at line widths of about 1 MHz. We decided to revisit the rotational spectrum of $c$-C$_2$H$_3$DO exactly because of these deviations.

evidence.loc: Discussion of the laboratory spectroscopic results
evidence.quote: The stronger transition frequencies are sufficiently accurate up to at least 1.5 THz which is sufficient for all astronomical observations dedicated to this isotopologue.

claims.hypothesis: Mono-deuterated oxirane (c-C2H3DO) is detectable towards IRAS 16293-2422 B in the ALMA PILS data, and its abundance traces the formation history of oxirane.
claims.experiment: Calculated LTE synthetic spectra using the new c-C2H3DO spectroscopy and fitted them to ALMA Band 7 (PILS) and Band 6 spectra of IRAS 16293-2422 B, supplemented by a rotation diagram analysis.
claims.result: Detected 24 transitions of c-C2H3DO, deriving T_rot = 103 +/- 19 K, column density = 8.9 x 10^14 cm^-2 (at 125 K) or (7.8 +/- 1.5) x 10^14 cm^-2 (rotation diagram), a c-C2H3DO/c-C2H4O ratio of ~0.15, and a D/H ratio of ~0.036 per H atom.
claims.finding: c-C2H3DO is firmly detected for the first time in the ISM; its intermediate D/H ratio (~0.036) suggests that oxirane forms fairly early during the evolution of prestellar cores.

evidence.quote: Fits of the detected lines using the rotation diagrams yield a temperature of $T_{\rm rot} = 103 \pm 19$ K, which in turn agrees well with 125 K derived for the $c$-C$_2$H$_4$O main isotopologue previously.

The $c$-C$_2$H$_3$DO to $c$-C$_2$H$_4$O ratio is found to be $\sim$0.15 corresponding to a D-to-H ratio of $\sim$0.036 per H atom which is slightly higher than the D-to-H ratio of species such as methanol, formaldehyde, ketene and but lower than those of the larger complex organic species such as ethanol, methylformate and glycolaldehyde. This may reflect that oxirane is formed fairly early in the evolution of the prestellar cores.

why_this_data.value: The PILS ALMA survey of IRAS 16293-2422 B provides high sensitivity and narrow lines (~1 km s^-1) at an offset position where continuum opacity is lower and absorption lines are weaker, minimizing line confusion for detecting rare deuterated isotopologues.

evidence.quote: Through the high sensitivity of PILS and narrow lines towards one component of IRAS 16293-2422 (limiting line confusion) a number of species have been detected for the first time
We focus on Source B in the present work because its narrow lines ($\sim$1 km s$^{-1}$) make it an ideal target for searches for rare species.

why_this_method.value: LTE synthetic spectrum fitting is appropriate because of the high gas densities in the protostellar envelope probed by ALMA, while a rotation diagram of unblended lines provides an independent check on T_rot and statistical uncertainties.

evidence.quote: The synthetic spectra were calculated assuming the molecules are in local thermodynamical equilibrium (LTE) which is sensible given the high densities in the molecular cloud surrounding the protostar that is probed by our ALMA observations (cite: PILS_overview_2016).
Such a rotation diagram may serve as a check of the modelling and it also provides a measure of the statistical uncertainties originating from the observational data.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using only previously published laboratory spectroscopy from (cite: c-C2H3DO_rot_2019) without new sub-mmW measurements; rejected because different choices of sextic distortion parameters caused ~0.2-0.3 MHz shifts in astronomical frequencies and small velocity offset deviations.

evidence.quote: While the data were extensive and accurate enough to identify $c$-C$_2$H$_3$DO with certainty in the PILS data we were faced with a small, but non-negligible deviation of the velocity offset in comparison to those of $c$-C$_2$H$_4$O and other molecules.

Releasing different sets of sextic distortion parameters resulted in transition frequencies that differed by around 0.2 MHz for the lines we had identified in our astronomical data, significant at line widths of about 1 MHz.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Watson's A reduction in the I^r representation vs S reduction in the III^l representation for the spectroscopic fit; both were fitted and presented, with S reduction in III^l favoured because it required two fewer parameters after adding 810-1060 GHz data.

evidence.loc: Observed spectrum and determination of spectroscopic parameters
evidence.quote: The inclusion of our transition frequencies in the 810$-$1060 GHz altered the situation; now the III$^l$ fit in the S reduction required two parameters less than the I$^r$ fit in the A reduction.

evidence.loc: Discussion of the laboratory spectroscopic results
evidence.quote: The parameter set in the III$^l$ representation employing Watson’s S reduction should be favoured over the set in the I$^r$ representation employing the A reduction because two fewer parameters are needed for a satisfactory fit.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Omitting all previously reported MW, mmW, and FIR transition frequencies from the global fit; rejected because retaining them slightly reduced parameter uncertainties (up to 10% for C).

evidence.loc: Observed spectrum and determination of spectroscopic parameters
evidence.quote: Omission of all previously reported transition frequencies changed the parameter values within the uncertainties and increased the parameter uncertainies only slightly; the largest increase occurred for the $C$ rotational parameter with slightly more than 10%. The previous transition frequencies were retained in the final fit nevertheless because their impact was not negligible.

limitations_admitted.value: In the Band 6 ALMA observations, only a small number of c-C2H3DO lines were covered and only one transition appeared to be unblended.

evidence.quote: We also applied our model based on the Band 7 data to the observations in Band 6: a small number of lines were detected in the more limited Band 6 data and only one appeared to be unblended (Fig. [5](#band6_figure)).

referee_caveats_inferred: The exact sky coordinates of the extracted spectrum towards IRAS 16293-2422 B and the assumed source size/continuum background temperature for the LTE synthetic modelling are not stated in this paper and must be retrieved from earlier PILS papers.
No uncertainty is quoted on the LTE model column density (8.9 x 10^14 cm^-2) or on the resulting D/H ratio (~0.036), although statistical uncertainties are given for the rotation diagram fit.

Source size and background continuum temperature assumed in the LTE radiative transfer calculation
Integrated line intensities (W or int T dV) of the individual unblended ALMA transitions used to construct the rotation diagram in Fig. 6
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Hundreds of GB to a few TB for the full PILS Band 7 survey (2013.1.00278.S) and Band 6 data (2016.1.01150.S), though <1 GB if using pre-extracted 1D spectra at the Source B offset position.
reproducibility.score_reason: The laboratory spectroscopy, line lists, SPFIT/SPCAT parameter files, CDMS predictions, and ALMA data are all publicly available, and the LTE/rotation diagram parameters (T_rot, FWHM, v_LSR) are clearly stated; however, the exact extraction coordinates, LTE source size/continuum treatment, and individual integrated line fluxes for the rotation diagram are not tabulated in the paper.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Both the ALMA data (projects 2013.1.00278.S and 2016.1.01150.S) and the CDMS spectroscopic catalog entry for c-C2H3DO are public, and the main astronomical results (T_rot = 103 +/- 19 K, N = 8.9e14 and 7.8e14 cm^-2, D/H = 0.036) are clear numeric targets derivable from standard LTE/rotation diagram analysis.

methods_papers.why: Pickett's SPFIT and SPCAT programmes used for fitting and calculating rotational transition frequencies.
Describes the Cologne submillimetre spectrometer system used for the laboratory rotational spectroscopy.

companion_papers.why: PILS survey overview paper describing the ALMA Band 7 observations and data reduction for IRAS 16293-2422.
Previous PILS detection and column density/temperature analysis of the main isotopologue c-C2H4O towards IRAS 16293-2422 B.
Presents the ALMA Band 6 observations and data reduction (2016.1.01150.S) used for additional line verification.
Recent rotational spectroscopy study of the main oxirane isotopologue (c-C2H4O) by the same group.
